<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE="-1" COLOR="GREEN"><A HREF="index.htm"><IMG SRC="img/tease.jpg"></A><BR><I>The Kojiki</I>, translated by Basil Hall Chamberlain, [1919], at sacred-texts.com</FONT></P><HR></p>  <h2 align="center">[SECT. LVI.&#8212;EMPEROR AN-NEI.]</h2>  
<p>His Augustness Shiki-tsu-hiko-tama-de-mi dwelt in the palace of Ukiana at Kata-shiha,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1059"></A><A HREF="#fn_1055"><FONT SIZE="1">1b</FONT></A> and ruled the Empire. This Heavenly Sovereign wedded Akuto-hime,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1060"></A><A HREF="#fn_1056"><FONT SIZE="1">2b</FONT></A> daughter of the Departmental Lord Haye,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1061"></A><A HREF="#fn_1057"><FONT SIZE="1">3b</FONT></A> elder brother of Kaha-mata-bime, and begot august children: His Augustness</p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p><a name="page_190"><font size="1" color="green">p. 190</font></A></p>  
<p><span class="contnote"><FONT SIZE=-2 COLOR=GREEN>[paragraph continues]</FONT></span> Toko-ne-tsu-hiko-irone,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1062"></A><A HREF="#fn_1058"><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT></A> next His Augustness Oho-yamato-hiko-suki-tomo,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1063"></A><A HREF="#fn_1060"><FONT SIZE="1">6</FONT></A> next His Augustness Shiki-tsu-hiko.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1064"></A><A HREF="#fn_1059"><FONT SIZE="1">5</FONT></A> Of the august children of this Heavenly Sovereign,&#8212;three Deities,&#8212;His Augustness Oho-yamato-hiko-suki-tomo [was he who afterwards] ruled the Empire. There were two Kings,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1065"></A><A HREF="#fn_1061"><FONT SIZE="1">7</FONT></A> children of the next [brother], His Augustness [155] Shiki-tsu-hiko. One child&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1066"></A><A HREF="#fn_1062"><FONT SIZE="1">8</FONT></A> (<small>was the ancestor of the Territorial Lords of Suchi in Iga,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1067"></A><A HREF="#fn_1063"><FONT SIZE="1">9</FONT></A> of the Territorial Lords of Nabari,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1068"></A><A HREF="#fn_1064"><FONT SIZE="1">10</FONT></A> and of the Territorial Lords of Minu</small>);&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1069"></A><A HREF="#fn_1065"><FONT SIZE="1">11</FONT></A> one child,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1070"></A><A HREF="#fn_1066"><FONT SIZE="1">12</FONT></A> His Augustness Wa-chi-tsumi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1071"></A><A HREF="#fn_1067"><FONT SIZE="1">13</FONT></A> dwelt in the palace of Miwi in Ahaji.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1072"></A><A HREF="#fn_1068"><FONT SIZE="1">14</FONT></A> So this King had two daughters: the name of the elder was Hahe-irone,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1073"></A><A HREF="#fn_1069"><FONT SIZE="1">15</FONT></A> and another name for her was Her Augustness Princess Oho-yamato-kuni-are:&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1074"></A><A HREF="#fn_1070"><FONT SIZE="1">16</FONT></A> the name of the younger was Hahe-irodo.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1075"></A><A HREF="#fn_1071"><FONT SIZE="1">17</FONT></A> The Heavenly Sovereign's august years were forty-nine. Augustness mausoleum est in privatis partibus Montis Unebi.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1076"></A><A HREF="#fn_1072"><FONT SIZE="1">18</FONT></A></p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>

<H3 ALIGN="CENTER">Footnotes</H3>
<P><A NAME="fn_1055"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1059">189:1b</A> In Kahachi: <i>uki-ana</i> signifies "floating hole," <i>Kata-shiha</i> is said to signify "hard rock" (<i>kata-iha</i>); but this seems doubtful, and the reading given by the characters in the text is not <i>Kata-shiha</i>, but <i>Kata-shiho</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1056"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1060">189:2b</A> <i>I.e.</i>, Princess of Akuto, or Akuta,&#8212;for the latter form of the name is more common. There exists a place thus called in Settsu. The derivation of the word is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1057"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1061">189:3b</A> <i>Agata-nushi-Haye</i>. The reading of this name is obscure, and its, derivation uncertain.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1058"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1062">190:4</A> <i>Irone</i> signifies "elder brother" or "elder sister." The rest of the compound is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1059"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1064">190:5</A> The first three elements of the compound signify "Great Yamato Prince." The last two are obscure, but Motowori identifies <i>suki</i> (see Note 3 to preceding Sect.)</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1060"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1063">190:6</A> <i>I.e.</i>, "Prince of Shiki"; so called, it is supposed, with reference to the place of residence of his grandfather.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1061"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1065">190:7</A> The character thus translated is <A NAME="img_19000"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/19000.jpg">, of which "King "is the original and proper signification. To judge by some other passages in the ancient histories, it had not yet in the 8th century altogether paled to <a name="page_191"><font size="1" color="green">p. 191</font></A> the lesser meaning of "prince," which has belonged to it in later times when denoting Japanese personages. It is still, as far as possible, used to denote the rulers of all countries excepting Japan, the zealous admirers of the native literature and institutions even designating by it the Emperor of China, who, one would have thought, had a special right to the more Honorific title of Emperor, which his own subjects were the first to invent. On the whole, therefore, "King "seems to be the most appropriate <A HREF="errata.htm#41">rendering</A>. The characters <A NAME="img_19100"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/19100.jpg"> are, by analogy, rendered "Queen."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1062"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1066">190:8</A> The text has "descendant"; but it must here be corrupt or at least faulty, as may be seen by the omission of the proper name.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1063"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1067">190:9</A> <i>Iga no Suchi no inaki</i>. The etymology of <i>Iga</i> and that of <i>Suchi</i> are alike obscure. See however Motowori's Commentary, Vol. XXI, p. 13, for the traditional derivation of the former. It is the name of a small province which in very ancient times formed part of the province of Ise.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1064"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1068">190:10</A> <i>Nabari no inaki</i>. Nabari is in Iga. The name signifies, "hiding."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1065"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1069">190:11</A> <i>Minu no inaki</i>. Minu, not to be confounded with the province of the same name, is a place in Iga. The name probably signifies "three moors."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1066"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1070">190:12</A> <i>I.e.</i>, the other child.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1067"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1071">190:13</A> Motowori reads <i>Chichitsumi</i>. In any case, the name remains obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1068"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1072">190:14</A> For Ahaji see Sect. VI, Note 3. <i>Mi-wi</i> signifies "august well," and the name is traced to the custom of bringing water from the Island of Ahaji for use in the Imperial Palace, as mentioned in Sect. CXXIX of the present work, and elsewhere in the early literature.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1069"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1073">190:15</A> <i>Irone</i> means "elder sister." <i>Hahe</i> is of uncertain import, it being written with completely different characters in the two histories.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1070"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1074">190:16</A> <i>Oho-yamato-kuni-are-hime-no-mikoto</i>. <i>Ono-yamato-kuni</i> signifies "the land of Great Yamato," and <i>hime</i> signifies "princess "or "maiden." Motowori suggests that <i>are</i>, which is an obscure word, may signify "pure."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1071"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1075">190:17</A> <i>Irodo</i> signifies "younger sister." For <i>hahe</i> <i>conf</i>. Note 15.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1072"></A><A HREF="kj063.htm#fr_1076">190:18</A> <i>Scil</i>. in interiori parte montis, <i>e.g.</i> in spelunca. Motowori explains the use of the term by reference to such words as foot, where the name of a portion of the human body is applied to a mountain. In Japanese there are others besides <i>ashi</i> ("foot"), such as <i>itadaki</i>, <i>hara</i> and <i>koshi</i>.</P>

<p>His Augustness Oho-yamato-hiko-suki-tomo dwelt in the palace of Sakahiwo at Karu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1077"></A><A HREF="#fn_1073"><FONT SIZE="1">1</FONT></A> and ruled the Empire. This Heavenly Sovereign wedded her Augustness Princess Futo-ma-waka,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1078"></A><A HREF="#fn_1074"><FONT SIZE="1">2</FONT></A> another name for whom was Her Augustness Princess Ihi-bi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1079"></A><A HREF="#fn_1075"><FONT SIZE="1">3</FONT></A> ancestress of the Departmental Lords of Shiki,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1080"></A><A HREF="#fn_1076"><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT></A> and begot august children: His Augustness Mi-ma-tsu-hiko-wake-shine,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1081"></A><A HREF="#fn_1077"><FONT SIZE="1">5</FONT></A> next His Augustness Tagishi-hiko&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1082"></A><A HREF="#fn_1078"><FONT SIZE="1">6</FONT></A> (<small>two Deities</small>). So His Augustness Mi-ma-tsu-hiko-kawe-shine [was he who afterwards] ruled the Empire. The next His Augustness Tagishi-hiko (<small>was the ancestor of the Lords of Chinu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1083"></A><A HREF="#fn_1079"><FONT SIZE="1">7</FONT></A> of the Lords of Take in Tajima,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1084"></A><A HREF="#fn_1080"><FONT SIZE="1">8</FONT></A> and of the Territorial Lords of Ashiwi</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1085"></A><A HREF="#fn_1081"><FONT SIZE="1">9</FONT></A> The Heavenly Sovereign's august years were forty-five. <P><A NAME="fn_1073"></A><A HREF="kj064.htm#fr_1077">192:1</A> <a name="page_192"><font size="1" color="green">p. 192</font></A> Karu, which still remains as a village in the province of Yamato, was famous down to the early historical days of Japan, being often mentioned by the poets. The derivation of the name is quite uncertain. <i>Sakahi-wo</i> probably signifies "boundary mound."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1074"></A><A HREF="kj064.htm#fr_1078">192:2</A> <i>Futo-ma-wakes-hime-no-mikoto</i>. The compound signifies "vast, true, and young princess."</P>

<P><A NAME="fn_1080"></A><A HREF="kj064.htm#fr_1084">192:8</A> <i>Tajima no Take no wake</i>. Motowori tells us that no mention of any place called Take in the province of Tajima is to be found in any other book.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1081"></A><A HREF="kj064.htm#fr_1085">192:9</A> <i>Ashiwi no inaki</i>. The same remark applies to this name as to the last. The two "gentile names" here mentioned are equally unknown except from this passage.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1082"></A><A HREF="kj064.htm#fr_1086">192:10</A> <i>Unebi-yama no Manago-dani</i>. It is in Yamato, and is now called Masago. The name signifies "a sandy place, or desert."</P>

<p><a name="page_193"><font size="1" color="green">p. 193</font></A></p>  <h2 align="center">[SECT. LVIII.&#8212;EMPEROR KO-SHO.]</h2>  
<p>His Augustness Mi-ma-tsu-hiko-kawe-shine dwelt at the palace of Waki-no-kami in Kadzuraki,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1087"></A><A HREF="#fn_1083"><FONT SIZE="1">1</FONT></A> and ruled the Empire. This Heavenly Sovereign wedded Her Augustness [157] Princess Yoso-taho,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1088"></A><A HREF="#fn_1084"><FONT SIZE="1">2</FONT></A> younger sister of Oki-tsu-yoso&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1089"></A><A HREF="#fn_1085"><FONT SIZE="1">3</FONT></A> ancestor of the Chiefs of Wohari,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1090"></A><A HREF="#fn_1086"><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT></A> and begot august children: His Augustness Ame-oshi-tarashi-hiko,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1091"></A><A HREF="#fn_1087"><FONT SIZE="1">5</FONT></A> and next His Augustness Oho-yamato-tarashi-hiko-kuni-oshi-bito&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1092"></A><A HREF="#fn_1088"><FONT SIZE="1">6</FONT></A> (<small>two Deities</small>). Now the younger brother, His Augustness Tarashi-hiko-kuni-oshi-bito [was he who afterwards] ruled the Empire. The elder brother His <A HREF="errata.htm#42">Augustness</A> Ame-oshi-tarashi-hiko (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Kasuga,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1093"></A><A HREF="#fn_1089"><FONT SIZE="1">7</FONT></A> the Grandees of Ohoyake,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1094"></A><A HREF="#fn_1090"><FONT SIZE="1">8</FONT></A> the Grandees of Ahata,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1095"></A><A HREF="#fn_1091"><FONT SIZE="1">9</FONT></A> the Grandees of Wonu;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1096"></A><A HREF="#fn_1092"><FONT SIZE="1">10</FONT></A> the Grandees of Kaki-no-moto,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1097"></A><A HREF="#fn_1093"><FONT SIZE="1">11</FONT></A> the Grandees of Ichihiwi;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1098"></A><A HREF="#fn_1094"><FONT SIZE="1">12</FONT></A> the Grandees of Ohosaka,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1099"></A><A HREF="#fn_1095"><FONT SIZE="1">13</FONT></A> the Grandees of Ana,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1100"></A><A HREF="#fn_1096"><FONT SIZE="1">14</FONT></A> the Grandees of Taki:&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1101"></A><A HREF="#fn_1097"><FONT SIZE="1">15</FONT></A> [158] the Grandees of Haguri,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1102"></A><A HREF="#fn_1098"><FONT SIZE="1">16</FONT></A> the Grandees of Chita,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1103"></A><A HREF="#fn_1099"><FONT SIZE="1">17</FONT></A> the Grandees of Muza;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1104"></A><A HREF="#fn_1100"><FONT SIZE="1">18</FONT></A> the Grandees of Tsunuyama,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1105"></A><A HREF="#fn_1101"><FONT SIZE="1">19</FONT></A> the Dukes of Ihitaka in Ise,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1106"></A><A HREF="#fn_1102"><FONT SIZE="1">20</FONT></A> the Dukes of Ichishi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1107"></A><A HREF="#fn_1103"><FONT SIZE="1">21</FONT></A> and the Rulers of the Land of Chika-tsu-Afumi</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1108"></A><A HREF="#fn_1104"><FONT SIZE="1">22</FONT></A></p>  
<p>The Heavenly Sovereign's august years were ninety-three. His August mausoleum is on Mount Hakata&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1109"></A><A HREF="#fn_1105"><FONT SIZE="1">23</FONT></A> at Waki-no-kami.</p>

<H3 ALIGN="CENTER">Footnotes</H3>
<P><A NAME="fn_1083"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1087">193:1</A> <a name="page_193"><font size="1" color="green">p. 193</font></A> In Yamato. The name of Waki-no-kami is of uncertain derivation. In the "Chronicles" the Emperor K&#333;-sh&#333; is said to have "dwelt at the palace of Ikegokoro at Waki-no-kami." For Kadzuraki see Sect. LV, Note 1.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1084"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1088">193:2</A> <i>Yoso-taho-bime-no-mikoto</i>. Here written phonetically, this name appears in the "Chronicles "written with characters to which the signification of "perfectly ornamented princess" should be attributed.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1085"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1089">193:3</A> The signification of this name is obscure, but it seems to be connected in some way with that of the other sister.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1086"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1090">193:4</A> <i>Wohari no murazhi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1087"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1091">193:5</A> <i>I.e.</i>, heavenly great perfect prince."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1088"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1092">193:6</A> <i>I.e.</i>, "great Yamato perfect prince, country great man." This name appears in an abbreviated form in the next sentence.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1089"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1093">193:7</A> <a name="page_194"><font size="1" color="green">p. 194</font></A><i>Kasuga na omi</i>. Kasuga is a celebrated place in the province of Yamato. The name is of uncertain origin, though the "Catalogue of Family Names" gives a story referring it to <i>Kasu gaki</i> (<A NAME="img_19400"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/19400.jpg">), <i>i.e.</i>, "lees fence." The curious combination of characters with which Kasuga is written,&#8212;<A NAME="img_19401"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/19401.jpg">&#8212;may be traced to the Pillow-Word <i>haru-hi no</i> (<A NAME="img_19402"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/19402.jpg">) which was not unnaturally prefixed to a name which so much resembled the Verb <i>kasumu</i>, "to be misty."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1090"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1094">193:8</A> <i>Ohoyake no omi</i>. Ohoyake is a place in Yamato. The name signifies "great granary."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1091"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1095">193:9</A> <i>Ahata no omi</i>. Ahata is a place in Yamashiro. The name signifies "millet-field."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1092"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1096">193:10</A> <i>Wonu no omi</i>. Wonu is a place in Afumi. The name signifies "little moor."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1093"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1097">193:11</A> <i>Kakinnomoto-uo-omi</i>. <i>Kaki-no-moto</i> signifies "at the bottom of the persimmon-tree," and the name is said by the compiler of the "Catalogue of Family Names" to have been granted to this family in allusion to a persimmon-tree which grew near their gate. This name was rendered illustrious in the eighth century by the poet Kakinomoto Hitomaro (See the present writer's "Classical Poetry of the Japanese," p. 217 of seq.).</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1094"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1098">193:12</A> <i>Ichihiwi no omi</i>. Ichihiwi is in Yamato. The name may signify "oak-well."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1095"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1099">193:13</A> <i>Ohosaka no omi</i>. Ohosaka is a place in Bingo. The name signifies "great hill, or pass."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1096"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1100">193:14</A> <i>Ana no omi</i>. Ana is a department in Bingo. The name signifies "hole" or "cave."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1097"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1101">193:15</A> <i>Taki no omi</i>. Taki is a district in Tamba. The name, which is a common one in Japan, means "water-falls."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1098"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1102">193:16</A> <i>Haguri no omi</i>. Haguri is a district in Wohari. The signification of the name is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1099"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1103">193:17</A> <i>Chita no omi</i>. Chita is a district in Wohari. The signification of the name is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1100"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1104">193:18</A> <i>Musa no omi</i>. Mudza is a district in Kadzusa. The name seems to be a corruption of the Chinese words <A NAME="img_19403"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/19403.jpg">, "warlike archer."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1101"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1105">193:19</A> <i>Tsunuyama no omi</i>. The family, the place, and the signification of the name are alike obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1102"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1106">193:20</A> <i>Ise no Ihitaka no kimi</i>. Ihitaka is the name of a district, and is traced to the signification of "abundant rice."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1103"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1107">193:21</A> <i>Ichishi no kimi</i>. Ichishi is a district in Ise. The signification of the name is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1104"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1108">193:22</A> <a name="page_195"><font size="1" color="green">p. 195</font></A> <i>Chika tsu Afumi no kuni-no-miyatsuko</i>. For Chika-tsu-Afumi see Sect. XXIX, Note 20.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1105"></A><A HREF="kj065.htm#fr_1109">193:23</A> In Yamato. The signification of the name is obscure.</P>

<p><a name="page_195"><font size="1" color="green">p. 195</font></A></p>  <h2 align="center">[SECT. LIX.&#8212;EMPEROR KOAN.]</h2>  
<p>His Augustness Oho-yamato-tarashi-hiko-kuni-oshi-bito dwelt in the palace of Akidzushima at Muro&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1110"></A><A HREF="#fn_1106"><FONT SIZE="1">1</FONT></A> in Kadzuraki, and ruled the Empire. This Heavenly Sovereign wedded his niece Her Augustness Princess Oshika,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1111"></A><A HREF="#fn_1107"><FONT SIZE="1">2</FONT></A> and begot august children: His Augustness Oho-kibi-no-moro-susumi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1112"></A><A HREF="#fn_1108"><FONT SIZE="1">3</FONT></A> next His Augustness, Oho-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-futo-ni&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1113"></A><A HREF="#fn_1109"><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT></A> (<small>two Deities</small>). So His Augustness Oho-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-futo-ni [159] [was he who afterwards] ruled the Empire. The heavenly Sovereign's august years were one hundred and twenty-three. His august mausoleum is on the Mound of Tamade.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1114"></A><A HREF="#fn_1110"><FONT SIZE="1">5</FONT></A></p>  
<p>

<H3 ALIGN="CENTER">Footnotes</H3>
<P><A NAME="fn_1106"></A><A HREF="kj066.htm#fr_1110">195:1</A> In Yamato. <i>Muro</i> signifies "cave" or "pit." <i>Aki-dzu-shima</i>, "the Island of the Dragon-Fly," is frequently used as an alternative name of Japan (see Sect. V, Note 26). See also the Emperor Y&#363;-riyaku's song given in Sect. CLVI.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1107"></A><A HREF="kj066.htm#fr_1111">195:2</A> <i>Oshika-hime-no-mikoto</i>. The name Oshika, which is obscure, appears in the "Chronicles" under the form of <i>Oshi</i>, which has generally been interpreted by Motowori (whom the translator follows) as a corruption of <i>ohoshi</i>, "great." This version of the name makes it harmonize with that of the Princess's father.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1108"></A><A HREF="kj066.htm#fr_1112">195:3</A> See Sect. LX, Note 11.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1109"></A><A HREF="kj066.htm#fr_1113">195:4</A> This name seems to signify "Great Yamato's Lord Prince, the Vast Jewel."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1110"></A><A HREF="kj066.htm#fr_1114">195:5</A> <i>Tamade no woka</i>. In Yamato. For this name see Motowori's Commentary, Vol. XXI, pp. 37-38.</P>

<p><a name="page_196"><font size="1" color="green">p. 196</font></A></p>  <h2 align="center">[SECT. LX.&#8212;EMPEROR K&#332;-REI.]</h2>  
<p>His Augustness Oho-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-futo-ni dwelt at the Palace of Ihodo at Kuruda,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1115"></A><A HREF="#fn_1111"><FONT SIZE="1">1</FONT></A> and ruled the Empire. This Heavenly Sovereign wedded Her Augustness Princess Kuhashi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1116"></A><A HREF="#fn_1112"><FONT SIZE="1">2</FONT></A> daughter of Ohome,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1117"></A><A HREF="#fn_1113"><FONT SIZE="1">3</FONT></A> ancestor of the Departmental Lords of Tohochi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1118"></A><A HREF="#fn_1114"><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT></A> and begot an august child: His Augustness Oho-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-kuni-kuru&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1119"></A><A HREF="#fn_1115"><FONT SIZE="1">5</FONT></A> (<small>one Deity</small>). Again he wedded Princess Chiji-haya-ma-waka of Kasuga,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1120"></A><A HREF="#fn_1116"><FONT SIZE="1">6</FONT></A> and begot an august child: Her Augustness Princess Chiji-haya&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1121"></A><A HREF="#fn_1117"><FONT SIZE="1">7</FONT></A> (<small>one Deity</small>). Again wedding Her Augustness Princess Oho-yamato-kuni-are,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1122"></A><A HREF="#fn_1118"><FONT SIZE="1">8</FONT></A> he begot august children: Her Augustness Yamato-to-mo-so-bime,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1123"></A><A HREF="#fn_1119"><FONT SIZE="1">9</FONT></A> next His Augustness Hiko-sashi-kata-wake;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1124"></A><A HREF="#fn_1120"><FONT SIZE="1">10</FONT></A> next His [160] Augustness Hiko-isa-seri-biko,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1125"></A><A HREF="#fn_1121"><FONT SIZE="1">11</FONT></A> another name for whom is His Augustness Oho-biki-tsu-hiko: next Yamato-to-bi-haya-waka-ya-hime&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1126"></A><A HREF="#fn_1122"><FONT SIZE="1">12</FONT></A> (<small>four Deities</small>). Again he wedded Haheirodo,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1127"></A><A HREF="#fn_1123"><FONT SIZE="1">13</FONT></A> younger sister of Her Augustness Princess Are, and begot august children,&#8212;His Augustness Hiko-same-ma,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1128"></A><A HREF="#fn_1124"><FONT SIZE="1">14</FONT></A> next His Augustness Waka-hiko-take-kibi-tsu-hiko&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1129"></A><A HREF="#fn_1125"><FONT SIZE="1">15</FONT></A> (two Deities). The august children of this Heavenly Sovereign [numbered] in all eleven Deities (<small>five kings and three queens</small>). So His Augustness Oho-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-kuni-kuru [was he who afterwards] ruled the Empire. The two Deities His Augustness Oho-kibi-tsu-hiko and His Augustness Waka-take-kibi-tsu-hiko together set sacred jars&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1130"></A><A HREF="#fn_1126"><FONT SIZE="1">16</FONT></A> at the front&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1131"></A><A HREF="#fn_1127"><FONT SIZE="1">17</FONT></A> of the River Hi&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1132"></A><A HREF="#fn_1128"><FONT SIZE="1">18</FONT></A> in Hari-ma;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1133"></A><A HREF="#fn_1129"><FONT SIZE="1">19</FONT></A> and, making Harima the mouth of the road,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1134"></A><A HREF="#fn_1130"><FONT SIZE="1">20</FONT></A> subdued and pacified the Land of Kibi. So His Augustness [161] Oho-kibi-tsu-hiko (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Kamu-tsu-michi in Kibi</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1135"></A><A HREF="#fn_1131"><FONT SIZE="1">21</FONT></A> The next, His Augustness Waka-hiko-take-kiki-tsu-hiko (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Shimo-tsu-michi in</small></p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>

<p><span class="contnote"><FONT SIZE=-2 COLOR=GREEN>[paragraph continues]</FONT></span> <small>Kibi&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1136"></A><A HREF="#fn_1132"><FONT SIZE="1">22</FONT></A> and of the Grandees of Kasa&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1137"></A><A HREF="#fn_1133"><FONT SIZE="1">23</FONT></A></small>). The next His Augustness Hiko-same-ma (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Uzhika in Harima&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1138"></A><A HREF="#fn_1134"><FONT SIZE="1">24</FONT></A></small>). The next, His Augustness Hiko-sashi-kata-wake (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Tonami in Koshi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1139"></A><A HREF="#fn_1135"><FONT SIZE="1">25</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Kunisaki in the Land of Toyo,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1140"></A><A HREF="#fn_1136"><FONT SIZE="1">26</FONT></A> of the Dukes of Ihobara,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1141"></A><A HREF="#fn_1137"><FONT SIZE="1">27</FONT></A> and of the Maritime Suzerains of Tsunuga</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1142"></A><A HREF="#fn_1138"><FONT SIZE="1">28</FONT></A> The Heavenly Sovereign's august years were one hundred and six. His august mausoleum is at Umasaka at Kotawoka.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1143"></A><A HREF="#fn_1139"><FONT SIZE="1">29</FONT></A></p>

<H3 ALIGN="CENTER">Footnotes</H3>
<P><A NAME="fn_1111"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1115">196:1</A> <a name="page_197"><font size="1" color="green">p. 197</font></A> In Yamato. <i>Iho-do</i> signifies "hut door." <i>Kuru-da</i> (<i>Kuroda</i> would be the more natural reading) signifies "black rice-field."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1112"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1116">196:2</A> <i>Kuhashi-hime-no-mikoto</i>. The name signifies "beautiful princess."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1113"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1117">196:3</A> This seems to have been originally not a personal name, but the name of a place in Wohari.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1114"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1118">196:4</A> <i>To-hochi no agata-mushi</i>. Tohochi is a district in Yamato. The name seems to signify "ten marts."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1115"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1119">196:5</A> This name signifies "great Yamato's lord prince who rules the land."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1116"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1120">196:6</A> <i>Kasuga no-chiji-haya-ma-waka-hime</i>. This name probably signifies "the thousand-fold brilliant truly young princess of Kasuga." For Kasuga see Sect, LVIII, Note 7.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1117"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1121">196:7</A> <i>Chiji-haya-hime-no-mikoto</i>, <i>i.e.</i>, probably "thousand-fold brilliant princess."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1118"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1122">196:8</A> <i>Oho-yamato-kuni-are-hime-no-mikoto</i>. See Sect. LVI, Note 16.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1119"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1123">196:9</A> Motowori assigns to this name the signification of "Yamato's hundred thousand-fold illustrious princess," and has a very long note on the subject in Vol. XXI, p. 42, <i>et seq</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1120"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1124">196:10</A> The signification of this name is not clear.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1121"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1125">196:11</A> <i>I.e.</i>, "prince valorously advancing prince." The alternative name signifies "Great Prince of Kibi," and both refer to his conquest of the province of Kibi as related a little further on in this Section. Motowori gives good reasons for supposing that <i>Oho-kibi-no-moro-susumi</i>, <i>i.e.</i> "He Who Completely Advances in Great Kibi," is but another form of the same name, erroneously inserted in the account of the preceding reign (see Sect, LIX, Note 3).</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1122"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1126">196:12</A> <i>I.e.</i>, perhaps "Yamato's hundred-fold wondrous brilliant young ornamental Princess." The name resembles that of the elder sister.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1123"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1127">196:13</A> For this and the next following names see Sect. LVI, Notes 17 and 16 respectively.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1124"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1128">196:14</A> <a name="page_198"><font size="1" color="green">p. 198</font></A> This name is obscure, and differs from that given in the parallel passage of the "Chronicles," where we read Sashima. The latter sounds more authentic.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1125"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1129">196:15</A> <i>I.e.</i>, "the young prince the brave prince of Kibi." This name refers to his conquest of Kibi, as related a few lines further on.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1126"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1130">196:16</A> <i>I.e.</i>, earthenware jars of a moderate size, probably intended to hold the rice-liquor offered to the gods, Being easily broken, they were planted in the ground up to a certain height.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1127"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1131">196:17</A> The probable meaning of this peculiar expression is "a bend in the river,"</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1128"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1132">196:18</A> Written with the character <A NAME="img_19800"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/19800.jpg">, "ice," which may however be only phonetic. No river of this name is anywhere else mentioned as flowing through the province of Harima, and one is tempted to suppose that there is some confusion with the celebrated river Hi, which figures so frequently in the Idzumo cycle of legends.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1129"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1133">196:19</A> One of the central provinces of Japan, on the northern shores of the Inland Sea. Some derive the name from <i>hagi-hara</i>, "lespedeza moor," while others, connect it with <i>hari</i>, a "needle," Neither etymology has much to recommend it.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1130"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1134">196:20</A> <i>I.e.</i>, "their point of departure." It must also be remembered that "road "came to have the sense of "circuit "or "province," so that we might translate this phrase by "the commencement of the circuit." <i>Conf</i>. such denominations as <i>Koshi no michi no kuchi</i>, <i>Koshi no michi no naka</i>, and <i>Koshi no michi no shiri</i> for what are in modern parlance the provinces of Echizen, Etchi&#363; and Echigo. The region nearest to the capital was called the mouth, while equally graphic designations were bestowed on the more remote districts. It was, as we learn by comparison with a passage in the history of the reign of the Emperor Su-jin (see Sect. LXVI, Note 13), customary thus to plant earthenware jars in the earth at the point whence an army started on an expedition, this being considered a means of invoking upon it the blessing of the gods. Not only so, but down to the Middle Ages travellers in general were in the habit of worshipping at the shrine of the god of roads. For "road" in the sense of "circuit," "province," or "administrative division "see Sect. LXVI, Note 2.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1131"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1135">196:21</A> <i>Kibi no kamu-tsu-michi no omi</i>. <i>Kamu-tsu-michi</i> <i>i.e.</i>, "the Upper Road "or "Circuit," was the ancient name of the province of Bizen (or of a portion of it), which formerly was a part of the Land of Kibi.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1132"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1136">197:22</A> <a name="page_199"><font size="1" color="green">p. 199</font></A> <i>Kibi no shimo-tsu-michi no omi</i>. <i>Shimo-tsu-michi</i> means "the lower road," and was the ancient name of a portion of the province of Bitchi&#363;, which formerly was a part of the land of Kibi.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1133"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1137">197:23</A> <i>Kasa no omi</i>, <i>i.e.</i>, "Grandees of the Hat," a "gentile name" which is referred by the compiler of the "Catalogue of Family Names" to an incident in the reign of the Emperor &#332;-jin, which he however by no means clearly relates (See Motowori's Commentary, Vol. XXI; p.p. 57-58).</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1134"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1138">197:24</A> <i>Harima no Uzhika no omi</i>. Uzhika is the name of a place. It is written with characters signifying "cow and deer," but the true derivation is quite uncertain.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1135"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1139">197:25</A> <i>Koshi no Tonami no omi</i>. Tonami is a district in Etchi&#363;. <A HREF="errata.htm#43">The</A> signification of the name is uncertain.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1136"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1140">197:26</A> <i>Toyo-kuni no Kunisaki no omi</i>. Kunisaki is a district in Bungo. The name seems to signify "land's end."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1137"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1141">197:27</A> <i>Ihobara no kimi</i>. Ihobara is a district in Suruga. The signification of the name is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1138"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1142">197:28</A> <i>Tsunuga no ama no atahe</i>. For Tsunuga see Sect. CI, Notes 3 and 12. Perhaps the name should rather be rendered "the Suzerains of Ama in Tsunuga," as Ama may, after all, as Motowori suggests, be here the name of a place.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1139"></A><A HREF="kj067.htm#fr_1143">197:29</A> In the Province of Yamato. <i>Kata-woka</i> signifies "side-mound" or "incomplete mound." <i>Uma-saka</i> signifies "horse-hill" or "horse-pass." Umasaka should perhaps be understood as the particular designation of a portion of the ascent of Katawoka, which is mentioned in the "Chronicles "as the name of a mountain.</P>

<p><a name="page_199"><font size="1" color="green">p. 199</font></A> [162]</p>  <h2 align="center">[SECT. XLI.&#8212;EMPEROR K&#332;-GEN.]</h2>  
<p>His Augustness Oho-yamato-ne-ko-hiko -kuni-kuru dwelt in the palace of Sakaki-bara at Karu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1144"></A><A HREF="#fn_1140"><FONT SIZE="1">1</FONT></A> and ruled the Empire. This heavenly Sovereign wedded Her Augustness Utsu-shiko-me,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1145"></A><A HREF="#fn_1141"><FONT SIZE="1">2</FONT></A> younger sister of His Augustness Utsu-shiko-wo,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1146"></A><A HREF="#fn_1142"><FONT SIZE="1">3</FONT></A> ancestor of the Grandees of Hodzumi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1147"></A><A HREF="#fn_1143"><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT></A> and begot august children: His Augustness Oho-biko,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1148"></A><A HREF="#fn_1144"><FONT SIZE="1">5</FONT></A> next His Augustness Sukuna-biko-take-wi-goro;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1149"></A><A HREF="#fn_1145"><FONT SIZE="1">6</FONT></A> next His Augustness Waka-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-oho-bibi&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1150"></A><A HREF="#fn_1146"><FONT SIZE="1">7</FONT></A> (<small>three Deities</small>).</p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>

<p><a name="page_200"><font size="1" color="green">p. 200</font></A></p>  
<p><span class="contnote"><FONT SIZE=-2 COLOR=GREEN>[paragraph continues]</FONT></span> Again, wedding Her Augustness I-gaka-shiko-me,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1151"></A><A HREF="#fn_1147"><FONT SIZE="1">8</FONT></A> daughter of His Augustness Utsu-shiko-wo, he begot an august child: His Augustness Hiko-futu-oshi-no-makoto.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1152"></A><A HREF="#fn_1148"><FONT SIZE="1">9</FONT></A> Again, wedding Princess Haniyasu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1153"></A><A HREF="#fn_1149"><FONT SIZE="1">10</FONT></A> daughter of Awotama&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1154"></A><A HREF="#fn_1150"><FONT SIZE="1">11</FONT></A> of Kafuchi, he begot an august child: His Augustness Take-hani-yasu-biko&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1155"></A><A HREF="#fn_1151"><FONT SIZE="1">12</FONT></A> (<small>one Deity</small>). The august children of this Heavenly Sovereign [numbered in all five Deities]. So His Augustness Waka-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-oho-bibi [was he who afterwards] ruled the Empire. The children of [163] his elder brother, His Augustness Oho-biko, were His Augustness Take-numa-kaha-wake&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1156"></A><A HREF="#fn_1152"><FONT SIZE="1">13</FONT></A> (<small>ancestor of the Grandees of Abe</small>);&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1157"></A><A HREF="#fn_1153"><FONT SIZE="1">14</FONT></A> next His Augustness Hiko-inakoshi-wake&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1158"></A><A HREF="#fn_1154"><FONT SIZE="1">15</FONT></A> (<small>This was the ancestor of the Butler Grandees.</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1159"></A><A HREF="#fn_1155"><FONT SIZE="1">16</FONT></A> His Augustness Hiko-futu-oshi-no-mikoto wedded Princess Takachina of Kadzuraki,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1160"></A><A HREF="#fn_1156"><FONT SIZE="1">17</FONT></A> young sister of Cho-nabi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1161"></A><A HREF="#fn_1157"><FONT SIZE="1">18</FONT></A> ancestor of the Chiefs of Wohari,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1162"></A><A HREF="#fn_1158"><FONT SIZE="1">19</FONT></A> and begot a child: the Noble Umashi Uchi.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1163"></A><A HREF="#fn_1159"><FONT SIZE="1">20</FONT></A> (<small>This was the ancestor of the Grandees of Uchi in Yamashiro.</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1164"></A><A HREF="#fn_1160"><FONT SIZE="1">21</FONT></A> Again, wedding Princess Yama-shita-kage,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1165"></A><A HREF="#fn_1161"><FONT SIZE="1">22</FONT></A> younger sister of Udzu-hiko,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1166"></A><A HREF="#fn_1162"><FONT SIZE="1">23</FONT></A> ancestor of the Rulers of the Lord of Ki,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1167"></A><A HREF="#fn_1163"><FONT SIZE="1">24</FONT></A> he begot a child, the Noble Take-Uchi&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1168"></A><A HREF="#fn_1164"><FONT SIZE="1">25</FONT></A> The children of this Noble Take-Uchi [numbered] in all nine (<small>seven males and two females</small>),&#8212; namely] the Noble of Hata-no-Yashiro,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1169"></A><A HREF="#fn_1165"><FONT SIZE="1">26</FONT></A> [who] (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Hata,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1170"></A><A HREF="#fn_1166"><FONT SIZE="1">27</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Hayashi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1171"></A><A HREF="#fn_1167"><FONT SIZE="1">28</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Hami,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1172"></A><A HREF="#fn_1168"><FONT SIZE="1">29</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Hoshikaha,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1173"></A><A HREF="#fn_1169"><FONT SIZE="1">30</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Afumi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1174"></A><A HREF="#fn_1170"><FONT SIZE="1">31</FONT></A> and of the Dukes of the Hatsuse Tribe</small>);&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1175"></A><A HREF="#fn_1171"><FONT SIZE="1">32</FONT></A> next the Noble Kose-no-Wo-Kara&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1176"></A><A HREF="#fn_1172"><FONT SIZE="1">33</FONT></A> [who] (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Kose,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1177"></A><A HREF="#fn_1173"><FONT SIZE="1">34</FONT></A> of the Grandees of the Sazaki Tribe,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1178"></A><A HREF="#fn_1174"><FONT SIZE="1">35</FONT></A> and of the Grandees of the Karu Tribe</small>);&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1179"></A><A HREF="#fn_1175"><FONT SIZE="1">36</FONT></A> next the Noble Soga no Ishikaha&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1180"></A><A HREF="#fn_1176"><FONT SIZE="1">37</FONT></A> [who] (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Soga,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1181"></A><A HREF="#fn_1177"><FONT SIZE="1">38</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Kahanobe,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1182"></A><A HREF="#fn_1178"><FONT SIZE="1">39</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Tanaka,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1183"></A><A HREF="#fn_1179"><FONT SIZE="1">40</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Takamuko,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1184"></A><A HREF="#fn_1180"><FONT SIZE="1">41</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Woharida&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1185"></A><A HREF="#fn_1181"><FONT SIZE="1">42</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Sakurawi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1186"></A><A HREF="#fn_1182"><FONT SIZE="1">43</FONT></A> and of the Grandees of Kishida</small>);&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1187"></A><A HREF="#fn_1183"><FONT SIZE="1">44</FONT></A> next the Noble Heguri-no-Tsuku,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1188"></A><A HREF="#fn_1184"><FONT SIZE="1">45</FONT></A></p>

<p><span class="contnote"><FONT SIZE=-2 COLOR=GREEN>[paragraph continues]</FONT></span> [who] (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Heguri,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1189"></A><A HREF="#fn_1185"><FONT SIZE="1">46</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Sawara,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1190"></A><A HREF="#fn_1186"><FONT SIZE="1">47</FONT></A> and of the Uma-mi-kuhi Chiefs</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1191"></A><A HREF="#fn_1187"><FONT SIZE="1">48</FONT></A> next the Noble Kino-Tsunu&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1192"></A><A HREF="#fn_1188"><FONT SIZE="1">49</FONT></A> [who] (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Ki,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1193"></A><A HREF="#fn_1189"><FONT SIZE="1">50</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Tsumu;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1194"></A><A HREF="#fn_1190"><FONT SIZE="1">51</FONT></A> and of the Grandees of Sakamoto</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1195"></A><A HREF="#fn_1191"><FONT SIZE="1">52</FONT></A> next Princess Mato of Kume;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1196"></A><A HREF="#fn_1192"><FONT SIZE="1">53</FONT></A> next Princess Nu-no-iro;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1197"></A><A HREF="#fn_1193"><FONT SIZE="1">54</FONT></A> next Kadzuraki-no-Nagaye-no-sotsu-biko&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1198"></A><A HREF="#fn_1194"><FONT SIZE="1">55</FONT></A> [who] (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Tamade,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1199"></A><A HREF="#fn_1195"><FONT SIZE="1">56</FONT></A> of the Grandees of Ikuha,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1200"></A><A HREF="#fn_1196"><FONT SIZE="1">57</FONT></A> of the Grandees [166] of Ikuye&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1201"></A><A HREF="#fn_1197"><FONT SIZE="1">58</FONT></A> and of the Grandees of Agina</small>),&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1202"></A><A HREF="#fn_1198"><FONT SIZE="1">59</FONT></A> moreover [there was] the Noble Waku-go&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1203"></A><A HREF="#fn_1199"><FONT SIZE="1">60</FONT></A> (<small>the ancestor of the Grandees of Yenuma</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1204"></A><A HREF="#fn_1200"><FONT SIZE="1">61</FONT></A> This Heavenly Sovereign's august years were fifty-seven. His august mausoleum is on the mound in the middle of the Pool of Tsurugi.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1205"></A><A HREF="#fn_1201"><FONT SIZE="1">62</FONT></A></p>

<H3 ALIGN="CENTER">Footnotes</H3>
<P><A NAME="fn_1140"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1144">199:1</A> <a name="page_201"><font size="1" color="green">p. 201</font></A> In Yamato. For Karu see Sect. LVII, Note I. <i>Sakahi-bara</i> signifies "boundary moor."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1141"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1145">199:2</A> <i>I.e.</i>, perhaps, "the beautiful but alarming female."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1142"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1146">199:3</A> <i>I.e.</i>, perhaps, "the beautiful but alarming male."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1143"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1147">199:4</A> <i>Hodzumi no omi</i>. There are several places called Hodzumi in various provinces. The name appears to signify "piling up rice-ears."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1144"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1148">199:5</A> <i>I.e.</i>, "great prince."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1145"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1149">199:6</A> <i>I.e.</i>, "little prince-fierce-boar-heart," the boar being known for its savage disposition.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1146"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1150">199:7</A> Excluding the last member of the compound, this name signifies "young-Yamato-lord-prince-great" <i>Bibi</i> is identified by Motowori with the word <i>mimi</i>, which so often recurs in proper names (see Sect. XIII, Note 18).</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1147"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1151">200:8</A> Motowori explains this name in the sense of "brilliant-alarming-female," but some doubt must attach to it.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1148"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1152">200:9</A> <i>I.e.</i>, perhaps, "prince vast-great-truth."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1149"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1153">200:10</A> <i>Hani-yasu-bime</i>. This name has already been met with in Sect. VII, Note 3. Motowori however supposes that in this place Haniyasu should be considered to be the name of a place in Yamato.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1150"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1154">200:11</A> <i>I.e.</i>, a man called "green jewel" who lived in the province of Kafuchi.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1151"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1155">200:12</A> <i>Take</i> signifies "brave." For the rest of the name see Note 10.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1152"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1156">200:13</A> <i>Take</i> signifies "brave." <i>Wake</i> is either "young" or "lord." For <i>Nuna-kaha</i> see Sect. LI, Note 31.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1153"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1157">200:14</A> <a name="page_202"><font size="1" color="green">p. 202</font></A> <i>Abe no omi</i>. There are several places called Abe, and it is doubtful to which of them the text here refers.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1154"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1158">200:15</A> The signification of <i>inakoshi</i> seems to be "rice-chariot". <i>Hiko</i> is "prince," and <i>wake</i> either "young "or "lord."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1155"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1159">200:16</A> <i>Kashihade no omi</i>, This name is traditionally referred to an incident in the reign of the Emperor Kei-ko, who is said to have bestowed it on one of his attendants who served up to him a particularly savoury dish of shell-fish. "Butlers" (perhaps the word might also be rendered "cooks") have been mentioned towards the end of Sect. XXXII, and again in the legend of Jim-mu's slaughter of the "earth-spiders "related in Sect. XLVIII.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1156"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1160">200:17</A> <i>Katsuraki-no-takachina-bime-no-mikoto</i>. The signification of <i>Takachina</i> is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1157"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1161">200:18</A> By aphaeresis for <i>Oho-inabi</i>, the form of the name given in the "Chronicles of Old Matters of Former Ages." itself perhaps standing by apocope for <i>Oho-ina-biko</i>, which would signify "great rice-prince."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1158"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1162">200:19</A> <i>Wohari no Murazhi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1159"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1163">200:20</A> <i>Umashi Uchi no sukune</i>. Umashi signifies "sweet," and <i>Uchi</i> is the name of a place in Yamashiro.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1160"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1164">200:21</A> <i>Yamashiro no Uchi no omi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1161"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1165">200:22</A> This name may be rendered literally "the shade beneath the mountains," but the signification is "the glow from the autumn leaves on the mountain-side."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1162"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1166">200:23</A> <i>I.e.</i>, probably "wonderful (or precious) prince."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1163"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1167">200:24</A> <i>Ki no kuni no miyatsuko no aya</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1164"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1168">200:25</A> <i>Take-Uchi no sukune</i>. <i>Take</i> signifies "brave," and <i>Uchi</i> is the name of a district in Yamato. The common, but erroneous, reading of this name is <i>Take no Uchi no sukune</i>. The celebrated personage, who may be styled the Methuselah of Japan, is said to have lived during the reigns of five Emperors, who themselves averaged over a hundred years of life each. His own age is variously given as 255, 260, etc. up to 360 years.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1165"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1169">200:26</A> <i>Hata no Yashiro no sukune</i>. <i>Hata</i> and <i>Yashiro</i> are supposed by Motowori to be the names of places in Yamato. <i>Yashiro</i> signifies "shrine." <i>Hata</i> is of uncertain derivation.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1166"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1170">200:27</A> <i>Hata no omi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1167"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1171">200:28</A> <i>Hayashi no omi</i>. Hayashi is the name of a place in Kawachi, and signifies "forest."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1168"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1172">200:29</A> <i>Hami no omi</i>. There is a Hami in Afumi and another in Tamba. The signification of the name is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1169"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1173">200:30</A> <a name="page_203"><font size="1" color="green">p. 203</font></A> <i>Hoshikaha no omi</i>. Hoshikaha is a place in Yamato. The name signifies "star river."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1170"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1174">200:31</A> <i>Afumi no omi</i>. For Afumi see Sect. XXIX, Note 20.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1171"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1175">200:32</A> <i>Hatsuse-be no Kimi</i>. For Hatsuse see Sect. CXLIII, Note 8.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1172"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1176">200:33</A> <i>Kose no Wo-kara no sukune</i>. Kose is the name of a place in Yamato. The meaning of Wo-kara is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1173"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1177">200:34</A> <i>Kose no omi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1174"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1178">200:35</A> <i>Sazakibe no omi</i>. See Sect. LIII, Note 10.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1175"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1179">200:36</A> <i>Kurube no omi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1176"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1180">200:37</A> <i>Soga no Ishikaha no sukune</i>. Soga is a place in Yamato, and Ishikaha a district in Kahachi. In cases like this it must generally be presumed that the family had two seats, or was divided into two branches residing in different places. Sometimes, however, the original seat and that to which the family afterwards removed are meant to be indicated.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1177"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1181">200:38</A> <i>Soga no omi</i>. The signification of Soga is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1178"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1182">200:39</A> <i>Kahanobe no omi</i>. Kahanobe is the name of a district in Settsu, and signifies "river-bank."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1179"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1183">200:40</A> <i>Tanaka no omi</i>. Tanaka is the name of a place in Yamato and signifies "among the rice-fields."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1180"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1184">200:41</A> <i>Takamuko no omi</i>. Takamuko seems to be the name of a place in Echizen. Its signification is uncertain.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1181"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1185">200:42</A> <i>Woharida no omi</i>. Woharida is a place in Yamato. The name seems to mean "little ploughed field."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1182"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1186">200:43</A> <i>Sakurawi no omi</i>. Sakurawi is the name of a place in Kahachi and signifies "cherry-tree well."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1183"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1187">200:44</A> <i>Kishida no omi</i>. Kishida is a place in Yamato. The signification of the name is not clear.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1184"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1188">200:45</A> <i>Heguri no Tsuku no sukune</i>. Heguri is the name of a district in Yamato, and is of uncertain signification. <i>Tsuku</i> (modern <i>dzuku</i>), "owl," is a name which is referred to a tradition that will be found in Motowori's Commentary, Vol. XXII, p. 29.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1185"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1189">201:46</A> <i>Heguri no omi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1186"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1190">201:47</A> <i>Sawara no omi</i>. Sawara was perhaps a district in Chikuzen. The signification of the name is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1187"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1191">201:48</A> <i>Uma mi-kuhi no murazhi</i>. The literal significance of the characters with which <i>Uma-mi-kuhi</i> is written is "horse august post." But whether this name had any relation to horses, or whether it should simply be regarded as the name of a place is quite uncertain.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1188"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1192">201:49</A> <i>Ki no Tsunu no sukune</i>. Ki is the name of a province, and <a name="page_204"><font size="1" color="green">p. 204</font></A> Tsunu that of a district in another province,&#8212;the province of Suhau (Suw&#333;). <i>Conf</i>. Note 37.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1189"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1193">201:50</A> <i>Ki no omi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1190"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1194">201:51</A> <i>Tsunu no omi</i>.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1191"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1195">201:52</A> <i>Sakamoto no omi</i>. Sakamoto is the name of a place in Idzumi and signifies "base of the hill."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1192"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1196">201:53</A> <i>Kume no Ma-ito-hime</i>. Kume may be, as Motowori says, the name of a place. But see Sect. XXXIV, Note 7. In any case the place, if it existed, was probably called after some person of the name of Kume. The signification of Ma-iro is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1193"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1197">201:54</A> <i>Nu-no-iro-hime</i>. The meaning of this name is obscure.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1194"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1198">201:55</A> Kadzuraki is the already frequently mentioned name of a district in Yamato, and Nagaye is likewise the name of a place,&#8212;whether in Yamato or in Kahachi is not certain. It signifies "long inlet." Motowori thinks that the syllable <i>so</i> in this place is the same as the of <i>kuma-so</i>, and signifies "valiant "or "fierce."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1195"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1199">201:56</A> <i>Tamade no omi</i>. There is a Tamade in Yamato and another in Kahachi. The signification of the name is uncertain.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1196"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1200">201:57</A> <i>Ikuha no omi</i>. The "Chronicles of Japan" tell us that the original form of this name <i>Ikuha</i> was <i>uki-ha</i>, <i>i.e.</i>, "floating leaf," and give a story to account for it. See Motowori's Commentary, Vol. XXII, pp. 36-37, where the reason traditionally given to explain the fact of the name Ikuha being written with the character <A NAME="img_20400"></A>
<IMG SRC="img/20400.jpg"> is also mentioned at length.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1197"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1201">201:58</A> <i>Ikuye no omi</i>. Ikuye must have been the name of a place; but nothing is known of it.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1198"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1202">201:59</A> Agina no anti. The same observation applies to this as to the preceding name.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1199"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1203">201:60</A> <i>Waku-go no sukune</i>. <i>Waku-go</i> signifies "young child "or youth," an Honorific designation.</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1200"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1204">201:61</A> <i>Yenuma no omi</i>. Yenuma is the name of a district in Kaga, and signifies "inlet-lagoon."</P>
<P><A NAME="fn_1201"></A><A HREF="kj068.htm#fr_1205">201:62</A> In Yamato. This pool or lake is often mentioned in the poems of the "Collection of a Myriad Leaves" and was celebrated for its lotus-flowers. We hear of it in the "Chronicles of Japan," as having been dug in the reign of the Emperor &#332;-jin, but it was probably, like many others, a natural pool or marsh, which was afterwards improved. The name signifies "sabre."</P>

<p><a name="page_205"><font size="1" color="green">p. 205</font></A></p>  <h2 align="center">[SECT. LXII.&#8212;EMPEROR KAI-KUWA.]</h2>  
<p>His Augustness Waka-yamato-ne-ko-hiko-&#333;ho-bibi dwelt in the palace of Izakaha at Kasuga,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1206"></A><A HREF="#fn_1202"><FONT SIZE="1">1</FONT></A> and ruled the Empire. This Heavenly Sovereign wedded the Princess of Takanu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1207"></A><A HREF="#fn_1203"><FONT SIZE="1">2</FONT></A> daughter of Yugori&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1208"></A><A HREF="#fn_1204"><FONT SIZE="1">3</FONT></A> the Great Departmental Lord of Taniha,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1209"></A><A HREF="#fn_1205"><FONT SIZE="1">4</FONT></A> and begot an august child: His [167] Augustness Hiko-yumusumi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1210"></A><A HREF="#fn_1206"><FONT SIZE="1">5</FONT></A> (<small>one Deity</small>). Again he wedded his step-mother, Her Augustness I-gaka-shiko-me,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1211"></A><A HREF="#fn_1207"><FONT SIZE="1">6</FONT></A> and begot august children: His Augustness Mima-kiri-biko-iniwe;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1212"></A><A HREF="#fn_1208"><FONT SIZE="1">7</FONT></A> next Her Augustness Mima-tsuhime&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1213"></A><A HREF="#fn_1209"><FONT SIZE="1">8</FONT></A> (<small>two Deities</small>). Again he wedded Her Augustness Oke-tsu-hime,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1214"></A><A HREF="#fn_1210"><FONT SIZE="1">9</FONT></A> younger sister of His Augustness Hiko-kuni-oketsu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1215"></A><A HREF="#fn_1211"><FONT SIZE="1">10</FONT></A> ancestor of the Grandees of Wani,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1216"></A><A HREF="#fn_1212"><FONT SIZE="1">11</FONT></A> and begot an august child: King Hiko-imasu&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1217"></A><A HREF="#fn_1213"><FONT SIZE="1">12</FONT></A> (<small>one Deity</small>). Again, wedding Princess Washi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1218"></A><A HREF="#fn_1214"><FONT SIZE="1">13</FONT></A> daughter of the Noble Kadzuraki-no-tarumi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1219"></A><A HREF="#fn_1215"><FONT SIZE="1">14</FONT></A> he begot an august child,&#8212;King Take-tayo-hadzura-wake&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1220"></A><A HREF="#fn_1216"><FONT SIZE="1">15</FONT></A> (<small>one Deity</small>); The august children of this Heavenly Sovereign [numbered] in all five Deities (four Kings and one Queen), So His Augustness Mi-maki-iri-biko-iniwe [was he who afterwards] ruled the Empire. The children of his elder brother, King Hiko-yumusumi were: King Oho-tsutsuki-tari-ne;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1221"></A><A HREF="#fn_1217"><FONT SIZE="1">16</FONT></A> next King Sanugi-tari-ne&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1222"></A><A HREF="#fn_1218"><FONT SIZE="1">17</FONT></A> (<small>two Kings</small>). There [168] were five Deities daughters of these two Kings. Next King Hiko-imasu wedded the Princess of Yena in Yamashiro,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1223"></A><A HREF="#fn_1219"><FONT SIZE="1">18</FONT></A> another name for whom was Kari-bata-tobe,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1224"></A><A HREF="#fn_1220"><FONT SIZE="1">19</FONT></A> and begot children: King Oh&#333;-mata;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1225"></A><A HREF="#fn_1221"><FONT SIZE="1">20</FONT></A> next King Wo-mata;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1226"></A><A HREF="#fn_1222"><FONT SIZE="1">21</FONT></A> next King Noble [of?] Shibumi&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1227"></A><A HREF="#fn_1223"><FONT SIZE="1">22</FONT></A> (<small>three Deities</small>). Again, wedding Saho-no-oho-kurami-tome,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1228"></A><A HREF="#fn_1224"><FONT SIZE="1">23</FONT></A> daughter of Take-kuni-katsu-tome, of Kasuga,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1229"></A><A HREF="#fn_1225"><FONT SIZE="1">24</FONT></A> he begot children: King Saho-biko;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1230"></A><A HREF="#fn_1226"><FONT SIZE="1">25</FONT></A> next King Wo-zaho;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1231"></A><A HREF="#fn_1227"><FONT SIZE="1">26</FONT></A> next Her Augustness Saho-bime,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1232"></A><A HREF="#fn_1228"><FONT SIZE="1">27</FONT></A> another name for whom is Sahaji-hime&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1233"></A><A HREF="#fn_1229"><FONT SIZE="1">28</FONT></A></p>

<p><span class="contnote"><FONT SIZE=-2 COLOR=GREEN>[paragraph continues]</FONT></span> (<small>Her Augustness Saho-bime here mentioned was consort of the Heavenly Sovereign Ikume</small>);&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1234"></A><A HREF="#fn_1230"><FONT SIZE="1">29</FONT></A> and King Muro-biko,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1235"></A><A HREF="#fn_1231"><FONT SIZE="1">30</FONT></A> (four Deities). Again, wedding Okinaga-no-midzu-yori-hime,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1236"></A><A HREF="#fn_1232"><FONT SIZE="1">31</FONT></A> daughter of the [169] Heavenly Deity Mikage,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1237"></A><A HREF="#fn_1233"><FONT SIZE="1">32</FONT></A> who is held in reverence by the deacons of Mikami in Chika-tsu-Afumi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1238"></A><A HREF="#fn_1234"><FONT SIZE="1">33</FONT></A> he begot children: King Tatatsu-michi-no-ushi, Prince of Taniha;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1239"></A><A HREF="#fn_1235"><FONT SIZE="1">34</FONT></A> next King Midzuho-no-ma-wa-ka;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1240"></A><A HREF="#fn_1236"><FONT SIZE="1">35</FONT></A> next King Kamu-oho-ne,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1241"></A><A HREF="#fn_1237"><FONT SIZE="1">36</FONT></A> another name for whom is King Yatsuri-iri-biko;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1242"></A><A HREF="#fn_1238"><FONT SIZE="1">37</FONT></A> next Midzuho-no-i-ho-yori-hime;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1243"></A><A HREF="#fn_1239"><FONT SIZE="1">38</FONT></A> next Mimi-tsu-hime;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1244"></A><A HREF="#fn_1240"><FONT SIZE="1">39</FONT></A> (<small>three Deities</small>). Again, wedding his mother's younger sister Her Augustness Woke-tsu-hime,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1245"></A><A HREF="#fn_1241"><FONT SIZE="1">40</FONT></A> he begot children: King Ma-wata of Oho-tsutsuki in Yamashiro;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1246"></A><A HREF="#fn_1242"><FONT SIZE="1">41</FONT></A> next King Hiko-osu;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1247"></A><A HREF="#fn_1243"><FONT SIZE="1">42</FONT></A> next king Iri-ne&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1248"></A><A HREF="#fn_1244"><FONT SIZE="1">43</FONT></A> (<small>two Deities</small>). Altogether the children of King Hiko-imasu [numbered] in all eleven Kings. So the children of the elder brother King Oho, mata were: King Ake-tatsu;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1249"></A><A HREF="#fn_1245"><FONT SIZE="1">44</FONT></A> next King Unakami&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1250"></A><A HREF="#fn_1246"><FONT SIZE="1">45</FONT></A> [170] (<small>two Deities</small>). This King Ake-tatsu (<small>was the ancestor of the Dukes of the Homuji Tribe in Ise&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1251"></A><A HREF="#fn_1247"><FONT SIZE="1">46</FONT></A> and of the Rulers of Sana in Ise</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1252"></A><A HREF="#fn_1248"><FONT SIZE="1">47</FONT></A> King Una-kami (<small>was the ancestor of the Dukes of Himeda.</small>&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1253"></A><A HREF="#fn_1249"><FONT SIZE="1">48</FONT></A> The next King Wo-mata (<small>was the ancestor of the Dukes of Magari in Tagima</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1254"></A><A HREF="#fn_1250"><FONT SIZE="1">49</FONT></A> The next King Noble Shibumi (was the ancestor of the Dukes of Sasa)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1255"></A><A HREF="#fn_1251"><FONT SIZE="1">50</FONT></A> The next King Saho-biko (<small>was the ancestor of the Chiefs of the Kusaka Tribe&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1256"></A><A HREF="#fn_1252"><FONT SIZE="1">51</FONT></A> and of the Rulers of the Land of Kahi</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1257"></A><A HREF="#fn_1253"><FONT SIZE="1">52</FONT></A> The next, King Wo-zaho (<small>was the ancestor of the Lords of Kadzunu&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1258"></A><A HREF="#fn_1254"><FONT SIZE="1">53</FONT></A> and the Lords of Kanu in Chika-tsu-Afumi.</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1259"></A><A HREF="#fn_1255"><FONT SIZE="1">54</FONT></A> The next King Muro-biko (<small>was the ancestor of the Lords of Mimi in Wakasa.</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1260"></A><A HREF="#fn_1256"><FONT SIZE="1">55</FONT></A> King Michi-no-ushi wedded the Lady Masu of Kahakami in Taniha,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1261"></A><A HREF="#fn_1257"><FONT SIZE="1">56</FONT></A> and begot children: Her Augustness Princess Hibasu;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1262"></A><A HREF="#fn_1258"><FONT SIZE="1">57</FONT></A> next Her Augustness Princess Matonu;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1263"></A><A HREF="#fn_1259"><FONT SIZE="1">58</FONT></A> next Her Augustness Oto-hime;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1264"></A><A HREF="#fn_1260"><FONT SIZE="1">59</FONT></A> next King Mi-kado-wake&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1265"></A><A HREF="#fn_1261"><FONT SIZE="1">60</FONT></A> (<small>four Deities</small>). This King Mikado-wake [171] (<small>was the ancestor of the Lords of Ho in Mikaha</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1266"></A><A HREF="#fn_1262"><FONT SIZE="1">61</FONT></A> Prince Midzuho-no-ma-waka, younger brother of this King Michi-no-ushi,</p>

<p><a name="page_207"><font size="1" color="green">p. 207</font></A></p>  
<p><span class="contnote"><FONT SIZE=-2 COLOR=GREEN>[paragraph continues]</FONT></span> (<small>was the ancestor of the Suzerains of Yasu in Chika-tsu-Afumi</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1267"></A><A HREF="#fn_1263"><FONT SIZE="1">62</FONT></A> The next, King Kamu-oho-be (<small>was the ancestor of the [Rulers of] the Land of Minu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1268"></A><A HREF="#fn_1264"><FONT SIZE="1">63</FONT></A> of the Rulers of the land of Motosu,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1269"></A><A HREF="#fn_1265"><FONT SIZE="1">64</FONT></A> and of the Chiefs of the Nagahata Tribe</small>)&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1270"></A><A HREF="#fn_1266"><FONT SIZE="1">65</FONT></A> The next, King Mawaka of Oho-tsutsuki in Yama-shiro wedded Princess Ajisaha of Mone,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1271"></A><A HREF="#fn_1267"><FONT SIZE="1">66</FONT></A> daughter of his younger brother Irine, and begot a child: King Kami-me-ikadzuchi.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1272"></A><A HREF="#fn_1268"><FONT SIZE="1">67</FONT></A> This King wedded Princess Takaki,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1273"></A><A HREF="#fn_1269"><FONT SIZE="1">68</FONT></A> daughter of the Grandee Tohotsu of Taniha&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1274"></A><A HREF="#fn_1270"><FONT SIZE="1">69</FONT></A> and begot a child: King Noble Okinaga.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1275"></A><A HREF="#fn_1271"><FONT SIZE="1">70</FONT></A> This king wedded the Princess of Takanuka in Kadzuraki,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1276"></A><A HREF="#fn_1272"><FONT SIZE="1">71</FONT></A> and begot children: Her Augustness Princess Okinaga-tarashi&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1277"></A><A HREF="#fn_1273"><FONT SIZE="1">72</FONT></A> next Her Augustness Sora-tsu-hime;&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1278"></A><A HREF="#fn_1274"><FONT SIZE="1">73</FONT></A> next King Prince Okinaga&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1279"></A><A HREF="#fn_1275"><FONT SIZE="1">74</FONT></A> (<small>three Deities. This [172] King was the ancestor of the Dukes of Homuji in Kibi,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1280"></A><A HREF="#fn_1276"><FONT SIZE="1">75</FONT></A> and of the Dukes of Aso in Harima</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1281"></A><A HREF="#fn_1277"><FONT SIZE="1">76</FONT></A> Again King Noble Okinaga wedded Princess Inayori of Kahamata&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1282"></A><A HREF="#fn_1278"><FONT SIZE="1">77</FONT></A> and begot a child: King Oho-tama-saka&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1283"></A><A HREF="#fn_1279"><FONT SIZE="1">78</FONT></A> (<small>This was the ancestor of the Rulers of the land of Tajima</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1284"></A><A HREF="#fn_1280"><FONT SIZE="1">79</FONT></A> The above-mentioned Take-toyo-hadzu-ra-wake (<small>was the ancestor of the Grandees of Chimori,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1285"></A><A HREF="#fn_1281"><FONT SIZE="1">80</FONT></A> of the Rulers of the Oshinumi Tribe,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1286"></A><A HREF="#fn_1282"><FONT SIZE="1">81</FONT></A> of the Rulers of the Mima Tribe,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1287"></A><A HREF="#fn_1283"><FONT SIZE="1">82</FONT></A> of the Oshinumi Tribe in Inaba,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1288"></A><A HREF="#fn_1284"><FONT SIZE="1">83</FONT></A> of the Lords of Takanu in Taniba,&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1289"></A><A HREF="#fn_1285"><FONT SIZE="1">84</FONT></A> and of the Abiko of Yosami</small>).&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1290"></A><A HREF="#fn_1286"><FONT SIZE="1">85</FONT></A> The Heavenly Sovereign's august years were sixty-three. His august mausoleum is at the top of the hill of Izakaha.&nbsp;<A NAME="fr_1291"></A><A HREF="#fn_1287"><FONT SIZE="1">86</FONT></A></p>  
<p>
</p>  
<p>
</p>
